patch.value: GH-1186: unrecoverable legacy merge-receipt references block strict health with diagnostic-only remediation

A fleet upgrade to pm 2026.9.3 exposes durable history references to receipts that older releases stored only in ignored clone-local runtime directories. Strict health blocks on merge_receipt_history_reference_missing, merge reconcile reports no pending work, and the remediation map points back to health diagnostics. The receipt was never committed and cannot be recovered in another clone.

Legacy clone-local-only receipt references are identified without weakening current receipt validation; a supported audited disposition or version-aware advisory can settle genuinely unrecoverable references; every blocking remediation demonstrably progresses state; schema_or_identity_invalid names the failed identity check and reports stable evidence provenance; mixed-version fleet fixtures and strict-exit negative controls cover the upgrade path
pm-cli 2026.9.3 upgrading repositories pinned between 2026.8.26 and 2026.8.31; Node 26.5.0; Linux

Open a repository whose historical merge_reconcile event references a receipt formerly written only under ignored runtime state; run pm merge reconcile --dry-run and then pm health --strict-exit --require-merge-drivers.
Every strict-health blocking finding has an executable, auditable remediation or a version-aware advisory classification when the historical evidence is provably unrecoverable.
Reconcile reports clean and changes nothing while strict health exits 1 for a missing reference; remediation_map names the diagnostic itself, leaving no state-progressing path.
